candidate.educational_objective: Interpret an elevated bilirubin as a nonspecific finding requiring correlation with bilirubin fractions and the clinical context.

options.A: Hyperbilirubinemia can result from increased bilirubin production, impaired hepatic handling/excretion, or biliary obstruction, so the pattern must be interpreted with the clinical context
options.B: An elevated bilirubin level in an adult is a normal finding that requires no further evaluation
options.C: Hyperbilirubinemia occurs only in newborns and has no meaningful differential diagnosis in adults
options.D: A total bilirubin elevation by itself identifies one specific liver disease

candidate.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories describes jaundice/hyperbilirubinemia as potentially arising from increased bilirubin production such as hemolysis, decreased excretion such as obstruction or hepatitis, or abnormal bilirubin metabolism. Total bilirubin alone is therefore not specific to one diagnosis.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports increased production, decreased excretion, and abnormal metabolism as mechanisms of hyperbilirubinemia and jaundice.
candidate.stem: An adult has jaundice and an elevated total bilirubin level. Which interpretation is most accurate?
